text:
maria: Heads-up — after the rc-2026.03.16 runtime merge we're seeing a ~22% token/sec drop on the continuous-batcher fleet in us-west. Queueing tails lengthened; small batches are getting stuck waiting for KV warmups. Flamegraphs attached to the thread (see link).
kevin: Ugh. Any obvious kernel fallbacks or memcopy spikes?
maria: Kernel selection appears stable, but memcopy syscall counts jump during the slow period. KV cache hit-rate falls ~12% on affected hosts. Numbers from a single host over a 10m window: total_tokens: 1.2M -> 950k, avg_tok_sec: 2000 -> 1560, p95_latency: 85ms -> 110ms.
ci-bot: perf/regression: CI job runtime-e2e/continuous-batcher (job 482) failed perf threshold: tokens/sec dropped 20% vs baseline. See https://ci.internal/jobs/482/logs
olivia: Can someone run a quick bisect across yesterday's merge set? If it's the prefetch/pacing heuristic change we should find it quickly.
hamid: Starting bisect now across commits 3f8a..d912 (those are the runtime merges landed yesterday).
hamid: bisection result: suspect commit d34b7e2 — touch to prefetch window and early-evict logic. Patch summary: "reduce prefetch aggressiveness; batch-victim early-evict to reduce memory pressure".
raj: That commit also adjusted KV warming timing to delay prefetch for short-seqlen requests. I'm seeing the KV hit-rate drop correlate with the same timestamps.
kevin: Can you paste the diff or the flag names? Want to try toggling on a prod-like host.
hamid: Diff snippet: ```diff --- a/scheduler/prefetch.cc +++ b/scheduler/prefetch.cc @@ -128,7 +128,7 @@ void Prefetcher::TryPrefetch(const Req& r) {- if (r.seqlen < PREFETCH_MIN_LEN) return;+ if (r.seqlen < PREFETCH_MIN_LEN && !r.is_priority) return;  // avoid prefetch on tiny non-priority reqs```
maria: So the change prevents prefetch for small non-priority requests. That seemed safe but in practice those tiny prompts were seeding the KV for subsequent continuation tokens from same user. Without them the next request misses cache and triggers heavier kernel work.
kevin: Check kernel fallback counters: are we seeing more fallbacks to slow memcpy path when KV miss causes larger sequence processing?
maria: Yes — kernel_fallback_count increments ~3x in the slow window. grep from one host: ```kernel_fallback_count: 37 -> 112 over 15m```
olivia: If bisect points at that commit, we can do either (A) revert the commit, (B) change rollout config to pin prefetch policy to previous behavior for affected clusters, or (C) tweak the early-evict threshold.
hamid: I pushed a quick diagnostic toggle to staging to re-enable prefetch for seqlen<4 regardless of priority. Running 30m smoke now.
hamid: Staging numbers after toggle: tokens/sec up +18%, KV hit-rate restored to ~prev levels, p95 latency down ~12%.
kevin: Good. Can we craft a short-term rollout fix while we design a better heuristic? Maybe add a `prefetch_min_dynamic` that scales with recent KV hit-rate per host.
raj: Agreed — adaptive prefetch would be ideal. For immediate rollback, I'm +1 for pinning old prefetch behavior on prod clusters until we ship an adaptive approach.
maria: I've put the rollout on HOLD and flagged the runtime release. @sre-bot please hold deploys for rc-2026.03.16 to prod until we decide. :warning:
sre-bot: Deploy hold placed on rc-2026.03.16 per request from maria. Reason: continuous-batcher token/sec regression and KV warmup interaction.
kevin: I'll prepare a tiny revert PR for d34b7e2 and run a canary on 3 hosts. If canary matches staging improvement we merge.
hamid: Bisect + staging toggle gives me confidence. I'll own the revert PR and test matrix for kernel fallback regression too.
maria: Thanks all. Action items: 1) hamid — open revert PR and run canary (ETA 45m). 2) kevin — draft adaptive prefetch proposal (short doc). 3) raj — gather KV hit-rate and kernel fallback metrics across clusters for postmortem. 4) olivia — coordinate rollback comms for impacted customers.
kevin: Adding small smoke command for canary run: ```./deploy_canary --cluster us-west-canary --image runtime:rc-2026.03.16-revert-d34b7e2 --check perf:tokens_per_sec,p95_latency --duration 30m```
maria: Leave this thread pinned to the release channel. I'll update when canary finishes. :thumbsup:
